name: AI-training and inference load profiles
applications: Capacity planning and utility interconnection requests for AI campuses
Cooling and power-train sizing for accelerator halls
Load forecasting and demand-flexibility product design
principle: AI workloads change the shape of a data centre's electrical load rather than only its size: training runs hold a large, sustained, synchronised draw across thousands of accelerators for hours, while inference is bursty and follows user traffic. Both run on accelerated servers whose share of the load is growing several times faster than conventional servers, so the design load is set by a rack density that air cooling cannot reach.

process_steps.name: Workload is scheduled (training job or inference traffic)
Accelerated servers draw power at rack level
Rack PDU and busway carry the load to the UPS and utility feed
Cooling removes the heat at the same density the rack produces it

key_equipment: rack PDUs rated for AI rack currents

performance.metric: growth rate of data centre electricity consumption
performance.basis: IEA: around 12 percent per year since 2017 (more than four times the growth of total electricity demand), accelerating to around 15 percent per year over 2024-2030.

source.note: IEA, Energy and AI, Energy demand from AI, read 2026-11-14

performance.metric: share of data centre electricity used by server equipment
performance.basis: IEA split: servers around 60 percent, storage around 5 percent, networking up to 5 percent, cooling about 7 percent for efficient hyperscale centres rising above 30 percent for less efficient enterprise centres.

source.note: IEA, Energy and AI, Energy demand from AI, read 2026-11-14

performance.metric: growth rate of accelerated-server electricity use against conventional servers
performance.basis: IEA: accelerated servers grow around 30 percent annually against 9 percent per year for conventional servers, and supply almost half of the net increase in data centre electricity use to 2030.

source.note: IEA, Energy and AI, Energy demand from AI, read 2026-11-14

advantages: Frames capacity planning around the load shape, not just annual energy
Explains why rack density, not floor area, now drives power and cooling design
Gives a defensible basis for interconnection requests and demand-flexibility products
limitations: The IEA pages read give no training-versus-inference split of energy demand
Per-accelerator power and shipment counts are not published on the pages read
Load shape varies by operator and is rarely disclosed
